title: Clinically unresponsive patients with acute brain injury activate a brain-computer interface
title_zh: 急性脑损伤患者在临床无反应状态下可激活脑机接口
abstract: Abstract Brain activation to verbal commands can be detected by EEG in clinically unresponsive patients. These patients with cognitive motor dissociation (CMD) are unable to communicate with the environment despite preserved consciousness. Advanced brain-computer interfaces (BCI) are promising to support motor function in patients with motor neuron disease or spinal cord injury. Our primary objective was to determine if clinically unresponsive patients can control a self-paced, one-way BCI early after acute brain injury. Secondarily, we assessed the association of BCI control with short- and long-term outcomes. We conducted a prospective single-centre cohort study in 41 clinically unresponsive, critically ill and acutely brain injured patients, as well as in a convenience sample of 8 healthy volunteers and 22 conscious critically ill patients. The self-paced BCI analysed EEG in real time and modulated frequency and pitch of a tone that patients controlled by attempting a motor task: patients were provided with instructions ‘to make the beep sound faster, keep opening and closing your right hand’ alternating with ‘to make the beep sound slower, stop opening and closing your right hand’. CMD was detected by applying machine learning to EEG recorded while patients listened to motor commands. Clinical outcomes were recovery of consciousness by hospital discharge, assessed with the Coma Recovery Scale–Revised, and recovery of functional independence at 12 months, defined as a Glasgow Outcome Scale–Extended score of 4 or higher (denoting the ability to function independently for 8 h or more). Additionally, we invited conscious patients as well as family members of conscious and clinically unresponsive patients to complete a survey on perceived utility and challenges associated with the BCI. In this study, 13 clinically unresponsive patients (32%) achieved BCI control and 8 of 41 (20%) were CMD-positive. All healthy volunteers and nine conscious patients (41%) were able to control the BCI. Median signal delay for BCI control was 49.8 [interquartile range (IQR) 39.9–75.6] seconds for clinically unresponsive patients, 17.1 (IQR 7.8–19.9) for conscious patients and 15.5 (IQR 12.9–21.2) for healthy volunteers. In the group of 41 clinically unresponsive patients, 4 of 13 patients with (31%) and 1 of 28 without BCI control (4%) recovered clinical consciousness at hospital discharge [odds ratio (OR) 21.2; 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.3–930.7]. At 12 months, 6 of 13 patients with (46%) and 2 of 28 without BCI control (7%) recovered functional independence (OR 9.9; 95% CI 1.8–81.6). None of the patients that were unable to control the BCI and were CMD-negative recovered. Patients with BCI control had shorter times to recovery of functional independence by 12 months than those who did not (hazards ratio 6.0; 95% CI 1.2–30.6). All respondents of the BCI survey (n = 37) expressed strong support for the potential future use of BCI devices. These results suggest that BCI control is a strong predictor of outcomes following acute brain injury and provide initial evidence that a bedside, EEG-based BCI system might permit bidirectional communication in critically ill unresponsive patients.
abstract_zh: 摘要：在临床无反应的急性脑损伤患者中，脑电图（EEG）可检测到对口头指令的脑激活。尽管意识保持，认知运动解离（CMD）患者无法与环境沟通。先进的脑机接口（BCI）有望支持运动神经元疾病或脊髓损伤患者的运动功能。本研究的主要目标是确定临床无反应患者在急性脑损伤后早期是否能控制自节奏、单向BCI。次要目标是评估BCI控制与短期和长期结果的关联。我们在41名临床无反应、危重且急性脑损伤患者中进行前瞻性单中心队列研究，并在8名健康志愿者和22名意识清醒的危重患者中进行便利样本研究。自节奏BCI实时分析EEG，并调节患者通过尝试运动任务控制的音调频率和音高：患者被指示“让蜂鸣声加快，持续张开和闭合右手”，交替“让蜂鸣声减慢，停止张开和闭合右手”。通过对患者在听取运动指令时记录的EEG应用机器学习检测CMD。临床结果包括出院时的意识恢复（使用修订版昏迷恢复量表评估）和12个月的功能独立性恢复，定义为格拉斯哥结果量表扩展版（GOS-E）得分≥4（表示能够独立功能8小时或以上）。此外，我们邀请意识清醒的患者以及意识清醒和临床无反应患者的家属完成关于BCI感知效用和挑战的调查。在本研究中，13名临床无反应患者（32%）实现了BCI控制，41名患者中有8名（20%）为CMD阳性。所有健康志愿者和9名意识清醒患者（41%）能够控制BCI。BCI控制的信号延迟中位数为49.8秒（四分位距39.9–75.6）对临床无反应患者，意识清醒患者为17.1秒（四分位距7.8–19.9），健康志愿者为15.5秒（四分位距12.9–21.2）。在41名临床无反应患者中，13名有BCI控制的患者中有4名（31%）在出院时恢复意识，28名无BCI控制的患者中有1名（4%）恢复意识（优势比21.2；95%置信区间2.3–930.7）。12个月时，13名有BCI控制的患者中有6名（46%）恢复功能独立性，28名无BCI控制的患者中有2名（7%）恢复功能独立性（优势比9.9；95%置信区间1.8–81.6）。未能控制BCI且CMD阴性的患者均未恢复。BCI控制的患者在12个月内实现功能独立性的时间比未控制者更短（风险比6.0；95%置信区间1.2–30.6）。BCI调查的所有受访者（n=37）均强烈支持BCI设备未来的潜在使用。这些结果表明，BCI控制是急性脑损伤后结果的强预测因子，并提供了初步证据，表明基于EEG的床旁BCI系统可能允许危重无反应患者进行双向沟通。
